question.leadin: Answer these questions about the attempted and successful killings of civil rights activists by the US government.
question.text: The FBI also sent this man a blackmail letter demanding that he commit suicide. This man delivered the "I Have a Dream" speech during the March on Washington.
question.clue: Robert Kennedy's impromptu speech in Indianapolis following this man's death probably kept the city from rioting.

swap.text: This lawyer successfully argued Brown before the Supreme Court. He became the first African-American justice on the Supreme Court in 1967.
swap.clue: His victories in Sweatt v. Painter and McLaurin v. Oklahoma State Regents opened up college access to previously disenfranchised applicants.

question.text: The Interstate Highway System was developed during the 1950s under this President, who was inspired by the Autobahn while Supreme Commander of Allied forces during World War II.
question.clue: His farewell address included a warning about the rising influence of the Military Industrial Complex.

swap.leadin: Give the following about the presidential Election of 1948.
swap.text: In the election, racist Strom Thurmond ran with this third party, whose common nickname is a mashup of"Democrat" and a term for the South. This party's official name was a political concept commonly cited inarguments for nineteenth-century slavery and twentieth-century segregation.
swap.clue: Strom Thurmond won four states running on the platform of this party, nicknamed for its southern origin. This party supported a bunch of segregationist policies.

question.leadin: In his dissenting opinion in this case, Justice Potter Stuart called a particular state's law regarding contraceptives "uncommonly silly."
question.text: Name this 1965 case in which the court ruled that a law banning contraceptives in that northeastern state interfered with an individual's right to privacy.
question.clue: The law under dispute in this case was a state statute of 1879 which even the dissenting justices, Hugo Black and Potter Stewart, agreed was "uncommonly silly."

swap.leadin: This organization was invited to participate in an event that saw protesters attempt to march from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama.
swap.text: Name this civil rights organization that was founded after the success of the Montgomery Bus Boycott, and whose members were attacked by policemen at the orders of "Bull" Connor.
swap.clue: At that time it had been led for four years by Ralph David Abernathy after the death of its founder.

question.leadin: Name some landmark U.S. court cases.
question.text: This 1963 case dealt with a Florida man convicted of breaking into the Bay Harbor Pool Room and ruled that not giving a convicted felon a right to counsel was unconstitutional.
question.clue: Losing attorney Bruce Jacob stated that his strategy in this case was to tie it to Betts v. Brady, which was overturned by this case.

swap.leadin: J. Edgar Hoover dubbed this movement "the greatest threat to the internal security" of the U.S.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary socialist group active throughout the 1970s in assessing and combating police brutality. Its members included founders Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale, as well as Angela Davis.
swap.clue: The Free Breakfast for Children program was founded by that U.S. group of this name, which was targeted by the Mulford Act to discourage its members' armed patrols of Oakland, which they called "copwatching."

question.leadin: Answer the following about advocacy efforts inspired by Vine Deloria Jr.
question.text: Deloria's book Custer Died for Your Sins heavily influenced this organization's founder, Russell Means. One member of this organization killed two FBI agents on Pine Ridge Reservation in 1975.
question.clue: It composed the Twenty Points during a campaign that ended with an occupation rife with vandalism of a Washington bureaucracy office building.

swap.text: When later asked about his casting the deciding vote in this 1986 case, Lewis Powell said, "I think I probably made a mistake on that one." Much maligned by gay rights groups, the ruling is likely to be overturned by the Supreme Court in the upcoming decision of Lawrence & Garner v. Texas. For 15 points-name this controversial Supreme Court case that upheld a Georgia law prohibiting homosexual sodomy.
swap.clue: The majority opinion argued that the First Amendment rights enumerated in Stanley v. Georgia did not extend to the facts of the case, though the dissent of Blackmun noted Stanley's Fourth Amendment implications.

question.leadin: This document is a counterpoint to the text titled "A Call for Unity."
question.text: Name this 1963 document, named for an Alabama location, in which the writer defends his civil disobedience. Its famous lines include "Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere" and it notably quotes Gladstone in saying "Justice too long delayed is justice denied."
question.answerHtml: Letter from Birmingham Jail [accept Letter from a Birmingham Jail, Letter from Birmingham City Jail, The Negro is Your Brother, accept modest variants]
question.clue: It was written in response to the statement "A Call for Unity" that urged the use of the court system rather than "direct action" led by outsiders.

swap.text: This Chicana activist worked with Cesar Chavez to cofound the United Farm Workers. She coined the UFW's slogan, "Si se puede" ("see say PWEH-day").
swap.clue: This activist co-founded the UFW with Chavez and coined the phrase "Si, se puede," which would later be translated and used during the 2008 election by Barack Obama.

question.leadin: Sixteen-year old Larry Kayne was shot for marching in support of this event.
question.text: Identify this 1968 event that began after the deaths of Echol Cole and Robert Walker. An activist delivered the "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech in support of this event at Mason Temple one day before his assassination.
question.clue: This event during which a group of predominantly African American workers walked off the job, much to the chagrin of Mayor Henry Loeb, a "white unity" advocate.

swap.text: The sit-in was first developed by Bernice Fischer, one of the co-founders of this organization. It was one of the "Big Four" of the civil rights movement along with the SCLC, SNCC ("snick"), and the NAACP.
swap.clue: Its second director retired in order to design a planned town called Soul City in North Carolina which quickly fell through.

question.text: Because Clifton's Cafeteria served people of all races, it was mentioned in this annual publication, which alternatively documented dangerous locations like "sundown towns."

swap.leadin: It was originally created after a series of sit-in protests in Greensboro North Carolina.
swap.text: Name this group whose leaders included Stokely Carmichael and Ella Baker.
swap.clue: Initially started in Greensboro, North Carolina, it was formally organized in a conference led by Ella Baker at Shaw University.

question.leadin: Answer the following about black voter suppression during Reconstruction.
question.text: Grandfather clauses, literacy tests, and this monetary measure were instituted in several Southern states to discourage blacks from registering to vote.
question.clue: Jim Crow laws forced African-Americans to pay these fees if they wanted to vote, until they were banned by the Twenty-Fourth Amendment.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian-American activism in the 20th century.
swap.text: This Japanese-American woman and her husband Bill pushed for reparations for internment camps. She took an iconic photo of Malcolm X after he was assassinated in the Audubon Ballroom.

question.text: Titles VIII and IX of the 1968 Civil Rights Act, which was signed during the riots, are commonly named for this issue. The Ink for Jack campaign arose from JFK's failure to use a "stroke of the pen" to address this issue, which was the focus of the Chicago Freedom Movement.
question.answerHtml: housing discrimination [accept fair housing or open housing; accept housing anti-discrimination; accept Fair Housing Act; prompt on descriptions of discrimination in the sale or rental of dwelling places; reject “public housing” or “affordable housing”]

swap.leadin: Identify the following about photographs depicting racism in the US.
swap.text: In this 1976 photograph by Stanley Forman, Joseph Rakes appears on the left wielding a flagpole against African-American lawyer Ted Landsmark during a protest against bussing in Boston.
